title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
description: Given a binary tree represented as an array in level-order (with `null` for missing nodes), return its maximum depth. A binary tree’s maximum depth is the number of nodes along the longest path from the root node down to the farthest leaf node. The array is in heap order: the children of the node at index `i` are at indexes `2i + 1` and `2i + 2`, and `null` means no node there.

hints.content: For array representation, node at index i has children at 2*i + 1 and 2*i + 2.
Recursive helper: function getDepth(i) { if (i >= tree.length || tree[i] === null) return 0; return 1 + Math.max(getDepth(2*i+1), getDepth(2*i+2)); }.

solution.explanation:
Recursive DFS traversal checking child nodes at 2i + 1 and 2i + 2.
Time Complexity: O(n)
Space Complexity: O(h) where h is tree height
